newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money eases to 10.0/11.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money eases to 10.0/11.0 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money eased to 10.0/11.0 percent from 14.0/15.0 percent on Friday morning following ample rupiah supply, dealers said.
They said the market was apparently well prepared and well supplied to meet the widely feared liquidity crunch on Friday due to the weekly tax payments, causing rates to fall.
Short-dated swaps softened and longer-term rates eased.
But dealers said the underlying fear extended to next Tuesday because of the mid-month factor when tax payments would reach their peak.

"We see overnight rates are falling. But people remain sceptical whether it could hold on. We will know better after lunch," one state bank dealer said, adding that liquidity could quickly turn around in the afternoon.
One Japanese bank dealer said operators were bidding for one-week money to bridge Monday and Tuesday as they expected possible tightening on those days.
One-week money was firmer at 12.00/12.25 percent and one-month at 12.50/12.75 percent.
The central bank kept its bilateral rates (SBIs) unchanged after lowering its three-month SBIs by 50 basis points on Thursday.
Bank Indonesia offered three-day SBIs at five percent, one-week at 6.5, two-week at 8.25, one-month at 10.25, three-month at 10.75, six-month at 11.5 and one-year at 12.0 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Thursday was 7.65 percent, compared with 11.24 percent on Wednesday.

One bond dealer said investors were choosy because of a variety of new issues coming to the market. Prices in the secondary market remained stable, with interest on Astra International bonds seen firming.
